title: Stochastic vs Batch Gradient Descent: Deep Learning Fundamentals

cues.en: -: Hello, and welcome back to the course on deep learning.
cues.zh: 講師：大家好，歡迎回深度學習。

cues.en: Today we're talk about stochastic gradient descent.
Previously we learned about gradient descent and we found out that it is a very efficient method to solve our optimization problem
cues.zh: 先前知道梯度下降很有效率，能解

cues.en: where we are trying to minimize the cost function.
cues.zh: 最小化成本的最佳化問題。

cues.en: It basically takes us from 10 to the power of 57 years to solving a problem within minutes or hours
cues.zh: 基本上把 10 的 57 次方年，變幾分鐘、幾小時，

cues.en: or within a day or so.
And it really helps speed things up because we can see which way is downhill and we can just go in that direction and take steps and get to the minimum faster.
cues.zh: 因能看下坡方向，往那走，更快到最小值。

cues.en: But the thing with gradient descent is that this method requires for the cost function to be convex.
cues.zh: 但這方法要求成本函數為凸。

cues.en: And as you can see here, we've specifically chosen a convex cost function.
Basically, convex means that the function looks similar to what we are seeing now that it's just convexed into one direction and that
cues.zh: 凸，基本上像目前，只朝一個方向彎，

cues.en: in essence has one global minimum and that's the one that we're going to find.
cues.zh: 本質只有一個全域最小值，要找的就是它。

cues.en: But what if our function is not convex?
What if our cost function is not convex?
What if it looks something like this?
Well, first of all, how could that happen?
Well, that could happen because if we first of all choose a cost function which is not the square difference
cues.zh: 可能選的成本，不是 ŷ 與 y

cues.en: between Y hat and Y, or if we do choose the cost function which is like that but then in a multidimensional space it can actually turn into something that is not convex.
cues.zh: 平方差；或即使選這種，多維空間也可能變非凸。

cues.en: And so what would happen in this case if we just tried to apply our normal gradient descent method, something like this could happen.
cues.zh: 這時套一般梯度下降，可能發生這樣。

cues.en: We could find a local minimum of the cost function rather than the global one.
cues.zh: 找到局部，不是全域最小。

cues.en: So this one was the best one and we found the wrong one and therefore we don't have the correct weights.
cues.zh: 這個才最好，但找到錯的，權重不正確。

cues.en: We don't have an optimized neural network.
We have a subpar neural network.
And so what do we do in this case?
Well, the answer here is stochastic gradient descent.
And it turns out the stochastic gradient descent doesn't require for the cost function to be convex.
So let's have a look at the two differences between the normal gradient that we talked about and the stochastic gradient descent.
cues.zh: 看看一般與隨機梯度下降的差異。

cues.en: So normal gradient descent is when we take all of our rows, we plug them into our neural network, and once again, here we've got the neural network copied over several times but the rows are being plugged
cues.zh: 一般取全部列，輸入網路；這裡網路複製多次，但每列都是輸入

cues.en: into that same neural network every time.
So there's only one neural network.
This is just for visualization purposes.
And then once we've plugged them in, we've calculated our cost function based on the formula on the right and looking at the chart at the bottom.
cues.zh: 全部輸入後，按右公式算成本，看底圖。

cues.en: And then we adjust the weights then, and this is called the gradient descent method or the proper term is the batch gradient descent method.
cues.zh: 再調權重，叫梯度下降，正式是批次梯度下降。

cues.en: So we take the whole batch from our sample, we apply it, and then we run that.
The stochastic gradient descent method is a bit different.
Here we take the row one by one.
So we take this row, we run our neural network and then we adjust the weights.
Then we move on to the second row.
We take the second row, we run our neural network, we look at the cost function and then we adjust the weights again.
cues.zh: 取第二、執行、看成本，再調。

cues.en: Then we take another row, take row three, we run our neural network, we look at the cost function, we adjust the weight.
So basically we are looking at, we're adjusting the weights after every single row rather than doing everything together and then adjusting the weights.
cues.zh: 每列後更新，不是全部一起完再調。

cues.en: Two different approaches and now we're going to just compare the two side by side.
So here they are, this is how to visually remember them.
So you've got the batch gradient descent where you're adjusting the weights after you've run them, after you've run all of the rows in your neural network.
cues.zh: 批次是網路跑完所有列後才調權重。

cues.en: And then basically you adjust the weights and you run the whole thing again, iteration, iteration, iteration.
In stochastic gradient descent method, you run one row at a time and you adjust the weights, you adjust the weights, you adjust the weights, and then you do everything again and again.
cues.zh: 隨機逐列，調、調、調，再全部重複。

cues.en: And that is called the stochastic gradient descent method.
The main two differences are that the stochastic gradient descent method helps you avoid the problem where you find those local extremas
cues.zh: 主要兩差異，它幫助避免只找到局部極值，

cues.en: or local minimums rather than the overall global minimum.
And the reason for that in simple terms is that the SGDM, the stochastic gradient descent method, has much higher fluctuations because it can afford them.
cues.zh: 簡單原因，SGD 波動更大，因承受得起。

cues.en: It's doing one iteration or one row at a time and therefore the fluctuations are much higher and it is much more likely to find the global minimum
cues.zh: 一次一列迭代，所以波動大，更可能找到全域，

cues.en: rather than just the local minimum.
And the other thing about the stochastic gradient descent method compared to the batch gradient is it's faster.
Like the first impression that you might have is because it's doing every single row one at a time It is slower, but actually in fact it is faster
cues.zh: 第一印象逐列較慢，實際更快，

cues.en: because it doesn't have to load up all the data into memory and wait until all of those rows are run altogether.
cues.zh: 因不用把全部載入記憶體，等所有一起跑。

cues.en: It can just run them one by one so it's much lighter algorithm, it's much faster in that sense.
Though it has way more, in those senses, it has more advantages over the batch gradient descent method, the main advantage or the main kind of like pro
cues.zh: 這些方面優勢多，但批次主要優點，

cues.en: for the batch gradient descent method is that it is a deterministic algorithm rather than stochastic gradient descent being a, stochastic algorithm meaning it's random.
cues.zh: 是確定式；隨機則是隨機演算法。

cues.en: And with the batch gradient descent method, as long as you have the same starting weights for your neural network, every time you run the batch gradient descent method, you will get the same
cues.zh: 批次只要初始權重相同，每次都得到同樣

cues.en: iterations, the same results for the way your weights are being updated first to have.
For the stochastic gradient decent method, you won't get that because it is a stochastic method.
You are picking your roles possibly at random and you are updating your neural network in a stochastic manner and therefore you are just going to every single time you run
cues.zh: 可能隨機挑列，隨機更新，所以每次跑

cues.en: the stochastic gradient decent method.
Even if you have the same weights at the start, you're going to have a different process, different iterations to get there.
cues.zh: 即使初始權重相同，到達結果的過程、迭代也不同。

cues.en: So that's in a nutshell what stochastic gradient descent is.
Also there's a method in between the two called the mini batch gradient descent method where you combine the two and you basically rather than running a whole batch or running one at a time,
cues.zh: 還有中間方法，小批次梯度下降，結合兩者，不跑整批、也不逐列，

cues.en: you run batches of rows, maybe five, 10, a 100, however millions you decide to set, you run that number of rows at a time, then you update your weights, and you update your weights and so on.
cues.zh: 而一批五、十、一百列，任你設定，每跑這些列就更新，再更新。

cues.en: And that's called the mini batch gradient descent method.
If you'd like to learn more about gradient descent, there's a great article which you can have a look at.
cues.zh: 想深入梯度下降，有篇好文。

cues.en: It's called "A Neural Network in 13 Lives of Python Part Two Gradient Descent" by Andrew Truk.
cues.zh: Andrew Trask 的 A Neural Network in 13 Lines of Python, Part 2: Gradient Descent。

cues.en: And the link is below, it's on GitHub, 2015 article.
Very well written in very simple terms.
It's got some interesting philosophical or just interesting thoughts on how to apply gradient descent, what are,
cues.zh: 一些有趣、哲學性想法，談如何應用、

cues.en: you know, the advantages and disadvantages and how to do things in certain situations.
So he's got some very cool tips, tricks and hacks.
Very easy read, so definitely check that out.
And another one, a bit more heavier read for those of you who are into mathematics or want to get to the bottom of the mathematics, why gradient descent in that specific,
cues.zh: 另一個較難，適合喜歡數學，或想徹底了解，為何梯度下降這樣，

cues.en: what are the formulas that are driving gradient, and how is it calculated, and so on check out the article or actually the book.
cues.zh: 背後公式、怎麼算，看看這文章，其實書。

cues.en: It's a free online book called "Neural Networks and Deep Learning" by Michael Nielsen.
cues.zh: 免費線上書 Neural Networks and Deep Learning，Michael Nielsen 著。

cues.en: 2015 book, it's just basically, it's all online.
You can go ahead and check it out there.
And they're, again, very soft introduction to the mathematics but the mathematics are pretty heavy as you go along, as you read through the article.
cues.zh: 數學入門平緩，但越讀越深入。

cues.en: But at the same time, it gets you into that mood.
cues.zh: 同時慢慢讓你進入狀況。

cues.en: I think even it has like a warm up chapter where you first warm up with the math and then you jump into them.
cues.zh: 我想還有暖身章，先數學暖身再深入。

cues.en: So interested in math, then this is the article to go to.
And there we go, so that's in a nutshell the difference between gradient descent and stochastic gradient descent and
cues.zh: 這就是一般與隨機梯度下降差異，

cues.en: how the two work.
And on that note, we're going to wrap up today's tutorial.
I look forward to seeing you on the next one.
And until then, enjoy deep learning.
cues.zh: 在那之前，祝你享受深度學習的樂趣。
